pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔢 **Strand 1 — Number**
Counting, calculating and reasoning with numbers — the language of trade, science and everyday life.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B7.1.4)
- B7.1.4.1 — Demonstrate an understanding of the concept of ratios and its relationship to fractions, and use it to solve problems that involve rates, ratios and proportional reasoning.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- write ratios and describe relationships using ratio language
- find and use unit rates
- make tables of equivalent ratios and share quantities in a given ratio
- use proportional reasoning to find missing values and plot pairs of values on a coordinate plane
- find a percentage of a quantity as a rate per 100 (commission, discount, interest)

pages.title: What is a ratio?
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Find ratio and use ratio language to describe the relationship between two quantities.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.4.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Ratio** — A **ratio** compares two quantities of the same kind measured in the same unit. The ratio of a to b is written **a : b** or as the fraction [[a/b]]. Like a fraction, a ratio can be simplified by dividing both terms by their HCF.
## ✏️ Example 4.1
There are 60 boys and 120 girls in a school. Find the ratio of boys to girls in its simplest form.
**Solution**
boys : girls = 60 : 120 = [[60/120]] = [[1/2]] = **1 : 2**
For every 1 boy there are 2 girls.
[[fig:m7-f16|Figure 4.1: A tape diagram of boys : girls = 1 : 2]]
## ✏️ Example 4.2
The ratio of wings to beaks in the bird house at the Kumasi Zoo is 2 : 1. Explain what this means.
**Solution**
Every bird has 2 wings and 1 beak, so **for every 2 wings there is 1 beak**. If there are 46 wings in the bird house, there are 23 beaks (23 birds).
## ✏️ Example 4.3
Alhasan is 50 years old and his son Musa is 25 years old. Describe their ages using ratio language.
**Solution**
Musa : Alhasan = 25 : 50 = **1 : 2**
Alhasan is **twice as old** as his son.
Musa is **half the age** of his father.
> ⚠️ **Watch out!** The order of a ratio matters. Boys : girls = 1 : 2 is not the same as girls : boys = 2 : 1. Also make sure both quantities are in the same unit before writing a ratio: 50 cm : 2 m = 50 cm : 200 cm = 1 : 4.

pages.title: Rates and unit rates
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use the concept of a unit rate associated with a ratio a : b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.4.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Rate and unit rate** — A **rate** compares two quantities measured in **different** units (e.g. kilometres per hour, cedis per kilogram). A **unit rate** tells how much of the first quantity there is for **one** unit of the second. For the ratio a : b, the unit rate is [[a/b]] of the first quantity per unit of the second.
## ✏️ Example 4.4
Write each as a unit rate.
a) A recipe has a ratio of 3 cups of flour to 4 cups of sugar.
b) Aisha polishes 8 square yards of floor tiles every 7 minutes.
**Solution**
a) [[3/4]] cup of flour **for each cup of sugar**.
b) [[8/7]] = 1[[1/7]] square yards **per minute**.
## ✏️ Example 4.5
If 2 litres of a soft drink cost GH₵18, find the cost of a) 1.5 litres b) 3 litres c) 7 litres.
**Solution**
Unit rate: GH₵18 ÷ 2 = **GH₵9 per litre**.
a) 1.5 × 9 = **GH₵13.50** b) 3 × 9 = **GH₵27** c) 7 × 9 = **GH₵63**
## ✏️ Example 4.6
At Salaga market, 3 kg of meat costs GH₵60. Complete the table.
| **Meat (kg)** | **2** | **3** | **5** | **12** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cost (GH₵) |  | 60 |  |  |
**Solution**
Unit rate: GH₵60 ÷ 3 = GH₵20 per kg.
| **Meat (kg)** | **2** | **3** | **5** | **12** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cost (GH₵) | 40 | 60 | 100 | 240 |

pages.title: Equivalent ratios and sharing in a given ratio
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Make tables of equivalent ratios (written as common fractions) relating quantities that are proportional.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.4.1.3
Equivalent ratios are made by multiplying or dividing every term of a ratio by the same number: 36 : 48 : 24 = 18 : 24 : 12 = 9 : 12 : 6 = 3 : 4 : 2.
## ✏️ Example 4.7
Kafui, Adoley and Jantuah shared an amount of money in the ratio of their ages. Kafui is 36 years old, Adoley 48 years and Jantuah 24 years. If Jantuah received GH₵24,000, how much money did they share?
**Solution**
| **Name** | **Equivalent ratios** |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kafui | 36 | 18 | 9 | 3 |
| Adoley | 48 | 24 | 12 | 4 |
| Jantuah | 24 | 12 | 6 | 2 |
Any column can be used. Using the simplest one, 3 : 4 : 2, the total number of parts is 3 + 4 + 2 = 9.
2 parts → GH₵24,000, so 1 part → GH₵12,000
9 parts → 9 × GH₵12,000 = **GH₵108,000**
They shared GH₵108,000 (Kafui GH₵36,000, Adoley GH₵48,000, Jantuah GH₵24,000).
[[fig:m7-f17|Figure 4.2: Tape diagram for sharing in the ratio 3 : 4 : 2]]
## ✏️ Example 4.8
Share GH₵350 between Aba and Esi in the ratio 3 : 4.
**Solution**
Total parts = 3 + 4 = 7. One part = GH₵350 ÷ 7 = GH₵50.
Aba: 3 × 50 = **GH₵150** Esi: 4 × 50 = **GH₵200**
Check: 150 + 200 = 350 ✓

pages.title: Proportional reasoning and graphs
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use proportional reasoning to find missing values in tables, and plot pairs of values on the coordinate plane.
Curriculum indicator B7.1.4.1.4
Two quantities are in **proportion** when their ratio stays the same. In a table of equivalent ratios, we can find a missing value by using the constant multiplier.
## ✏️ Example 4.9
Find the missing values x and y in the table of equivalent ratios.
| **First quantity** | **3** | **6** | **9** | **y** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Second quantity | 10 | x | 30 | 40 |
**Solution**
[[x/6]] = [[10/3]] ⟹ x = [[10/3]] × 6 = [[60/3]] = **20**
[[y/40]] = [[3/10]] ⟹ y = [[3/10]] × 40 = **12**
## ✏️ Example 4.10
Plot the pairs (3, 10), (6, 20), (9, 30) and (12, 40) on a coordinate plane. What do you notice?
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f18]]
Figure 4.3: Pairs of equivalent ratios lie on a straight line through the origin
All the points lie on a **straight line that passes through the origin (0, 0)**. This is true for every pair of quantities that are in proportion. We can read other values from the line, e.g. when the first quantity is 4.5, the second is 15.

pages.title: Percentage as a rate per 100
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g. 30% of a quantity means [[30/100]] times the quantity).
Curriculum indicator B7.1.4.1.5
> 🔑 **Key idea: Percent** — **Per cent** means "per hundred". 30% = [[30/100]], so 30% of a quantity means [[30/100]] × the quantity.
## ✏️ Example 4.11
A salesman is paid 35% commission. How much commission does he make on sales of GH₵700?
**Solution**
Commission = [[35/100]] × 700 = **GH₵245**
## ✏️ Example 4.12
Yaw paid GH₵80 for a shirt that was on sale at a discount of 20%. What was the original price?
**Solution**
After a 20% discount Yaw pays 100% − 20% = 80% of the original price.
80% of original = GH₵80 ⟹ original = 80 ÷ [[80/100]] = 80 × [[100/80]] = **GH₵100**
## ✏️ Example 4.13
A mobile phone which normally sells for GH₵450 is on sale at 40% off. How much would you pay for it?
**Solution**
Discount = [[40/100]] × 450 = GH₵180.
Price paid = 450 − 180 = **GH₵270** (or 60% of 450 = 270)
## ✏️ Example 4.14
A woman put GH₵520 into a savings account for one year. The rate of interest was 6% per year. How much was the interest for the year?
**Solution**
Interest = [[6/100]] × 520 = **GH₵31.20**
> 🌍 **Maths in real life** Shops use percentages for discounts, banks for interest, and businesses for commission. Always ask: "percentage **of what**?"

pages.title: Chapter 4 summary
pages.body:
- A ratio a : b compares quantities of the same kind; simplify by dividing by the HCF.
- A unit rate is the amount for one unit (e.g. GH₵9 per litre).
- To share in a ratio: add the parts, find one part, then multiply.
- Proportional pairs lie on a straight line through the origin.
- x% of Q = [[x/100]] × Q. Discount reduces a price; commission and interest are earned.
